Order:

-
The petitioners are aggrieved by the unilateral action of the 2nd respondent authority in holding out threats of demolition and dispossession of the petitioners from their respective properties.
2. It is submitted that the 2nd respondent in order to widen the road, intends to dispossess the petitioners vide notice dated 29.11.2025, calling upon the petitioners to execute a registered gift deed and also express consent for accepting the TDR bonds at 1:4 ratio for the land surrendered by the petitioners.

The petitioners are also called upon to submit the copies of the registered sale deed,
link documents, Aadhar Card photo copy, PAN Card photo copy and other documents to the 2nd respondent for determining the eligibility for grant of compensation/ TDR bonds.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that under the guise of the said notices, the 2nd respondent intends to issue TDR bonds, which are not acceptable to the petitioners.

4. Sri A.S.C. Bose, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent on instructions submits that the petitioners are initially offered TDR bonds on par with the other land owners whose property is also affected in the road widening process.
Now, that the petitioners have expressed their unwillingness to accept TDR bonds, in view of their extents of land affected in the road widening.

However, the respondent-authorities shall follow due process of law as laid down under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, if they intend to dispossess the petitioners from their property.

sentences.text: 5. Recording the same, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
